title: Building Reliable Support Agents Using the Effect Typescript Library - Michael Fester
talk_summary: A CTO of an AI support platform describes using the Effect TypeScript library to structure agent workflows (planner + actions + deterministic workflows + sub-agents) with typed schemas, dependency injection, retry policies, and provider fallback. The transferable content is architectural patterns for reliability and testability, not measured results; the talk is largely library advocacy with no benchmarks.

takeaways.technique: Stateful provider fallback with retry policies
takeaways.what_they_do: When an LLM provider fails, they fall back to a provider with similar performance characteristics, and the retry policy tracks state so it does not retry a provider already known to be failing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we fall back to another provider with similar performance characteristics... retry policies which also track state. So, we avoid retrying fail providers

takeaways.technique: Dependency injection to mock model providers and simulate failures
takeaways.what_they_do: Services are provided at the entry point and can be swapped for mock versions, so they test agent logic against simulated provider failures without touching internals.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we make heavy use of dependency injection to mock LM providers and simulate failure scenarios

takeaways.technique: Separate deterministic workflows from non-deterministic planner steps
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents are planners that choose actions/workflows/sub-agents, while workflows are deterministic multi-step processes (e.g. cancel subscription: collect reason, offer retention, check eligibility, cancel).
They define input, output, and error schemas up front with runtime validation and encoding/decoding, giving type safety and auto-generated docs across the stack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we define input, output, and error types up front. And those schemas come with powerful encoding and decoding built in

takeaways.technique: Duplicate token streams for live output plus storage
takeaways.what_they_do: Streamed answers are duplicated: one stream to the user, one persisted for analytics.

takeaways.technique: Structured error modeling to avoid swallowed failures
takeaways.what_they_do: They model errors explicitly in types but warn that it is easy to accidentally catch errors upstream and silently lose important failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's easy to accidentally catch errors somewhere upstream or out of sight and silently lose important failures
